content: For children aged 6 to 12 years, the recommended dosage is to swallow one tablet daily or every six hours. For individuals over 12 years of age, the dosage is 1250 mg taken orally with 8 ounces of water every six hours, not exceeding a total of 6 grams per day. Alternatively, the same dosage of 1250 mg with 8 ounces of water can be taken once daily or every six hours, again not exceeding 6 grams per day. Polycarbophil reduces the levels of demeclocycline, doxycycline, minocycline, oxytetracycline, and tetracycline by inhibiting their gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both polycarbophil and these medications. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended when these drugs are co-administered. Additionally, polycarbophil may decrease the effects of sodium picosulfate through an unspecified interaction mechanism. While this interaction is considered minor with unknown clinical significance, close monitoring is still advised. Potential side effects of polycarbophil include abdominal fullness, flatulence, vomiting, stomach cramps, hypersensitivity reactions, bowel obstruction, appendicitis, dysphagia, fecal impaction, and rectal bleeding. Taking this product without adequate fluid intake may cause it to swell and block the throat or esophagus, potentially leading to choking. Individuals with difficulty swallowing should not take this product. If symptoms such as chest pain, vomiting, difficulty swallowing, or breathing difficulties occur after taking this product, immediate medical attention should be sought. Consult a physician before using this product if you experience abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, or a sudden change in bowel habits lasting more than two weeks. If you are taking other medications, consult a healthcare professional, as laxatives like polycarbophil may affect the absorption and efficacy of other drugs. It is recommended to take this product at least two hours before or after other medications. Do not use this product for more than seven days unless directed by a physician. Discontinue use and consult a physician if rectal bleeding occurs or if you fail to have a bowel movement after using this or other laxatives, as these could be signs of a serious condition. Keep this product out of the reach of children. In case of overdose, seek medical help or contact a poison control center immediately. Regarding pregnancy, polycarbophil is not absorbed systemically and is considered safe for use during pregnancy. It is classified as Pregnancy Category A, meaning controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. For lactating women, there is no available data, but since polycarbophil is not absorbed, it is expected to be safe for use during breastfeeding.
